title: Generalize gcd_complete_characterization to any Euclidean domain

problemStatement.formal: theorem linear_combination_iff_gcd_dvd {R} [EuclideanDomain R] [DecidableEq R] (a b c : R) : (∃ x y, a * x + b * y = c) ↔ gcd a b ∣ c
problemStatement.plain: COMPLETED: Bézout's identity and the GCD characterization generalize from ℤ to any Euclidean domain. The key is EuclideanDomain.gcd_eq_gcd_ab which gives Bézout coefficients. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: linear_combination_iff_gcd_dvd and gcd_complete_characterization_ED proved in BezoutIdentityOQ04OQ02.lean. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
builtItems: gcd_achievable_ED: ∃ x y, ax+by = gcd(a,b) via gcd_eq_gcd_ab (lines 40-42)
IsBezout instance: every EuclideanDomain is IsBezout via inferInstance (line 89)
insights: EuclideanDomain is the right abstraction: UFD is insufficient (ℤ[X] counterexample: gcd(2,X)=1 but 1∉{2f+Xg})
EuclideanDomain.gcd_eq_gcd_ab provides explicit Bézout coefficients gcdA, gcdB
simp_rw [linear_combination_iff_gcd_dvd] reduces complete characterization to pure divisibility
The proof is remarkably concise: 4 lines each direction using Mathlib's extended GCD
nextSteps: Can linear_combination_iff_gcd_dvd be stated for IsBezout rings (without Euclidean structure)?
gcd in IsBezout is not unique — need to work with associates or choose a canonical representative
